initiative.summary: Group and sequence faults from a diagram review so agent diagrams stand on their own.
initiative.next_action: Start M1 (version readout) and M2 (heading budget)

sources.anchor: request: title, subtitle, extra note; diagrams should stand on their own
follow-up: PR stack may already fix some; show live version in status bar
7 repro files rendered identically on main d72e684

claims.statement: Diagrams must stand on their own with little prose
Long subtitle sets frame width; wrap it
Avoid unanchored explanatory notes; skill currently invites them
Legend must cover every color and explain dashed vs solid; allow horizontal legend
Long edge labels wrap; labels not at bends
Removed items in diffs stay readable (ghost, not heavy strike)
Sequence renders have canvas-colored patches and too many cards/borders
Accept small node shifts for straight lines between columns
Wide single-row drawings may need to fold; verify on main
Sidebar resize exists on main (#367), unreleased
Never commit private diagram content; use generic repros

shape.appetite: a few days of stacked PRs, one per group
shape.problem: Agent diagrams carry extra prose and visual codes the reader cannot decode
shape.recommended_shape: Seven groups A-G; skill and check fixes before renderer tuning; layout last
success_moves: Generic repro files give a before/after for each PR
Fix the skill and add a check warning so agents stop writing prose
Verify each fault on latest main before work (done at d72e684)
Diff ghost decided from a variant contact sheet
Layout work gated by the diagram-quality audit loop

first_proof.question: Does wrapping the subtitle shrink the frame to the drawing?
first_proof.decision_rule: If the frame shrinks, A owns the width fault; otherwise fault 4 owns it

rabbit_holes: Engine changes for straight columns colliding with the Arrange/Compare stack
open_decisions: Unanchored notes: warning only or removed later

deployment_surfaces: npm release via Version Packages PR #322
